title: Transaction-Specific Purpose and Mutuality
where_to_look: Review the preamble, Purpose definition, and permitted-use provisions.
required: Require a transaction-specific Purpose with expressly mutual disclosure and use solely for that Purpose.
fallback: Accept a broader defined business-relationship Purpose only if disclosure and use rights remain expressly mutual and Purpose-limited.
escalate_if: Escalate any blank or malformed Purpose, one-way disclosure or use rights, or use beyond the identified transaction.
flag_if: The Purpose contains a blank or unresolved placeholder.
The Purpose is not tied to an identified transaction or business relationship.
The NDA authorizes disclosure by only one party.
The use restriction does not expressly limit use solely to the Purpose.
The Purpose permits use for unrelated business activities.
preferred_language: Each party may disclose Confidential Information to the other solely to evaluate and pursue [describe transaction] (the “Purpose”), and each receiving party shall use the other party’s Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and disclose it only to its Representatives with a need to know for the Purpose.
confidence_note: Based on 27 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is consistently toward defined transaction scope and reciprocal coverage.
matching_clause_names: Purpose and Use of Confidential Information
Purpose Definition and Confidential Information Scope

title: Confidential Information Exclusions and Carve-Outs
where_to_look: Confidential Information definition and the exclusions or exceptions immediately following it.
required: Require customary exclusions for public information, documented prior possession, lawful third-party receipt, and independent development by or for Recipient without use or reference.
fallback: Accept customary carve-outs with reasonable-knowledge treatment for third-party source rights, while retaining no-fault public-domain and no-use protections.
escalate_if: Escalate deletion of customary exclusions, an exception allowing use of Confidential Information, or coverage of information obtained through a known breach.
flag_if: The definition of Confidential Information has no express exclusions.
The independent-development exclusion omits a no-use or no-reference condition.
The third-party-source exclusion lacks a lawful-source or no-confidentiality-duty condition.
The public-domain exclusion applies to information made public through Recipient's act or omission.
The prior-possession exclusion lacks a written-records requirement.
preferred_language: Confidential Information excludes information that is publicly available or later becomes publicly available through no act or omission of Recipient or its Representatives; was in Recipient’s possession on a non-confidential basis before disclosure, as shown by written records; was lawfully received from a third party that, to Recipient’s reasonable knowledge, had no duty to Disclosing Party restricting that disclosure; or was independently developed by or for Recipient without use of or reference to Confidential Information and without breach of this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 63 findings across multiple counterparties, consistent direction toward customary carve-outs with tighter proof and no-use conditions, although most changes were moderate.
matching_clause_names: Exceptions to Confidential Information — Compelled Disclosure

title: Confidential Information Definition, Scope and Designation
where_to_look: Look in the definitions section for the Confidential Information or Proprietary Information definition and designation mechanics.
required: Require coverage of non-public information related to the Purpose in any form, including unmarked, observed, inspected, and reasonably confidential information.
fallback: Accept marking or oral-identification mechanics only if observed information and reasonably confidential unmarked information remain protected.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that omits standard exclusions, protects unrelated information, or makes marking the sole basis for confidentiality.
flag_if: The definition makes written marking or designation the sole condition for protection.
The definition excludes information learned by observation or inspection.
The definition is not limited to information related to the Purpose, Transaction, or business relationship.
The definition omits employee, personal, affiliate, or third-party information where those categories are exchanged.
The clause is malformed or contains an unexplained cross-reference affecting scope.
preferred_language: “Confidential Information” means all non-public information related to the Purpose disclosed or made available by or on behalf of Discloser, in any form or medium, whether written, oral, electronic, visual, or learned through observation or inspection, whether or not marked or identified as confidential, that a reasonable person familiar with the industry and the circumstances would understand to be confidential. Confidential Information includes business, technical, financial, customer, supplier, employee, personal, affiliate, and third-party information, and all notes, analyses, compilations, and other materials that contain, reflect, or derive from it.
confidence_note: Based on 56 findings, direction is consistently toward broad, Purpose-linked coverage, with oral designation mechanics mixed.

title: Party Identification and Signature Blocks
where_to_look: Review the preamble, party definitions, notice details, and execution blocks.
required: Require each party’s exact legal name, entity type, formation jurisdiction, address, and matching signature-block name, with affiliates identified expressly.
fallback: Accept the exact legal name and matching signature block, while noting missing address or formation details for completion in the notices section.
escalate_if: Escalate any unresolved placeholder, uncertain legal name, mismatch between the party description and signature block, or change in affiliate scope.
flag_if: A party name field contains a blank, placeholder, or underscore line.
The party name differs between the preamble and the signature block.
The agreement omits an entity type or formation jurisdiction.
A party address is blank or incomplete.
Affiliates are added to or removed from the defined party.
preferred_language: Each party to this Agreement is identified by its full legal name, entity type, jurisdiction of formation, and principal or notice address, and each signature below is made on behalf of and binds the entity identified by that same full legal name.
confidence_note: Based on the supplied findings across numerous counterparties, this is a consistent, predominantly high-significance position.

title: Compelled and Required Disclosure Procedures
where_to_look: Look in legal-compulsion exceptions, subpoena response provisions, and required-disclosure procedures.
required: Require legally permissible prompt notice, Discloser-funded protective efforts, minimum necessary disclosure, and confidentiality assurances.
fallback: Accept a legally permissible notice duty and reasonable cooperation, while retaining minimum-necessary disclosure and confidentiality-assurance obligations.
escalate_if: Escalate if notice is eliminated, disclosure exceeds legal necessity, or Recipient must fund Discloser’s protective action.
flag_if: The notice duty lacks a legally permissible qualifier.
The clause omits a prompt written notice requirement.
The clause permits disclosure beyond the portion counsel advises is required.
The clause omits reliable assurances of confidential treatment.
The Recipient must pay for the Discloser’s protective order or other remedy.
preferred_language: If Recipient is required by law, regulation, subpoena, court order, or other legal process to disclose Confidential Information, Recipient shall, to the extent legally permissible, promptly notify Discloser in writing so Discloser may, at Discloser’s sole expense, seek a protective order or other remedy. Recipient shall reasonably cooperate with Discloser at Discloser’s expense, disclose only the portion and to the persons its legal counsel advises it must disclose, and use reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurances that the disclosure will receive confidential treatment.
confidence_note: Based on 86 findings across numerous counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward legally permissible notice, Discloser-funded protection, and minimum necessary disclosure.

title: Affiliate Scope and Receipt-Based Obligations
where_to_look: Affiliate and Representative definitions and provisions governing disclosure to Affiliates.
required: Define Affiliates by ownership or control and limit Representative status and obligations to Affiliates that receive Confidential Information from or at a Party’s direction.
fallback: Accept a broader Affiliate definition only if non-recipient Affiliates are not Representatives or obligors and the signing Party remains responsible for recipient Affiliates.
escalate_if: Escalate if any Affiliate is automatically bound or deemed a Representative without receiving Confidential Information.
flag_if: The Affiliate definition lacks a stated ownership or control threshold.
The draft deems every Affiliate a Representative.
The draft imposes obligations on an Affiliate without receipt of Confidential Information.
The draft extends enforcement rights to Affiliates without a receipt-based trigger.
preferred_language: “Affiliate” means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party through ownership of more than 50% of the voting interests or the power to direct management; notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no Affiliate shall be deemed a Party’s Representative or have any obligations under this Agreement unless it receives Confidential Information from or at the direction of a Party, and each Party remains responsible for the performance of its Affiliates that receive Confidential Information.
confidence_note: Based on 51 clause-name variants, the direction is highly consistent and predominantly high significance.

title: Return, Destruction and Retention of Confidential Information
where_to_look: Return, destruction, retention, and termination provisions for Confidential Information.
required: Require prompt return or destruction upon request or termination, with only a one-copy legal-retention exception and a narrow non-segregable-backup exception, while confidentiality continues.
fallback: Accept one archival copy and routine backups retained under a documented legal, compliance, or retention policy if access is restricted and confidentiality continues.
escalate_if: Do not accept unrestricted retention, use or disclosure of retained information, indefinite retention, or any lapse in confidentiality without attorney approval.
flag_if: The clause requires return or destruction upon request or termination.
The clause permits retention of one copy for legal, regulatory, compliance, audit, or document-retention purposes.
The clause excuses deletion of information not reasonably capable of being located or segregated.
The clause addresses routine disaster backups or ordinary-course backup servers.
The clause states that retained information remains confidential during retention.
preferred_language: Upon written request or termination of this Agreement, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information and, upon request, certify such destruction; provided that the Receiving Party may retain one copy of Confidential Information and anything deriving therefrom to the extent required for legal, regulatory, compliance, audit, or document-retention purposes, and may retain Confidential Information and anything deriving therefrom that is not reasonably capable of being readily located or segregated, including routine disaster backup media of email or electronic data. All retained information shall remain confidential for the period of retention and shall be destroyed in the ordinary course of business.
confidence_note: Based on 61 findings across multiple counterparties, consistent direction toward narrow retention exceptions with continuing confidentiality.

title: Purpose-Limited Use, Need-to-Know Disclosure, and Controlled Copying
where_to_look: Confidentiality sections addressing permitted use, Representatives, affiliates, third-party disclosure, and copying.
required: Require Purpose-only use, need-to-know disclosure to bound Representatives, consent for other third parties, responsibility for breaches, and Purpose-only copying.
fallback: Accept Purpose-only use and copying, need-to-know disclosure to Representatives bound by equally protective duties, and prompt notice for other disclosures with responsibility for breaches.
escalate_if: Escalate any use beyond the Purpose, unrestricted affiliate or third-party access, unprotected Representative access, or copying unrelated to the Purpose.
flag_if: Use is allowed outside the defined Purpose.
Disclosure is allowed to affiliates or Representatives without a need-to-know limit.
Representatives are not bound by confidentiality duties no less protective than the NDA.
The Receiving Party is not responsible for Representatives’ breaches.
Copying or transcription is allowed without a Purpose limitation.
preferred_language: Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose. It may disclose Confidential Information only to its employees, affiliates, agents, contractors, and professional advisers who have a bona fide need to know and are bound by this Agreement or written obligations no less protective than this Agreement, and Receiving Party shall be responsible for their breaches. Receiving Party may copy or transcribe Confidential Information only as necessary for the Purpose, and all copies shall remain Confidential Information. Any other disclosure requires Disclosing Party’s prior written consent.
confidence_note: Based on 43 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is consistent toward purpose-limited use, controlled need-to-know disclosure, Representative accountability, and Purpose-only copying.

title: Confidentiality Survival and Trade Secret Duration
where_to_look: Review the Term, Survival, and confidentiality-duration provisions following the confidentiality or non-use obligations.
required: Require confidentiality and non-use obligations to survive termination or expiration for five years, with trade secrets protected while they qualify.
fallback: Accept a three-year post-termination or post-expiration period only if trade secrets remain protected while they qualify under applicable law.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that omits post-termination survival or limits trade-secret protection to a fixed period.
flag_if: Confidentiality obligations end at termination or expiration.
The ordinary survival period is less than five years.
Trade-secret protection ends on a fixed date.
The clause leaves ordinary confidentiality obligations indefinite without a defined survival period.
The clause contains conflicting fixed and indefinite survival periods.
preferred_language: The obligations of confidentiality and non-use shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement for five years from the date of such termination or expiration. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information that qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law shall remain confidential for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret.
confidence_note: Based on 47 findings, the direction is highly consistent on trade-secret duration and consistently favors a defined three- to five-year period for ordinary information.

title: Agreement Term and Termination Rights
where_to_look: Term, termination, and survival provisions addressing expiration and post-termination confidentiality.
required: Require a defined term of no more than two years, mutual termination on 30 days’ written notice, and post-termination confidentiality survival.
fallback: Accept a defined term of up to three years with mutual written termination rights, provided confidentiality survives at least three years and trade secrets remain protected while they qualify as trade secrets.
escalate_if: Escalate if the term is perpetual or termination is one-sided or immediate. Escalate if confidentiality survives less than three years or trade secrets lack continuing protection.
flag_if: The agreement has no fixed expiration date.
Only one party may terminate the agreement.
Termination is effective immediately or without written notice.
Confidentiality obligations survive for less than three years.
Trade secrets lack protection while they qualify as trade secrets.
preferred_language: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and expire two (2) years thereafter unless terminated earlier by either Party upon thirty (30) days’ written notice to the other Party. The confidentiality obligations shall survive termination or expiration for three (3) years, and trade-secret Information shall remain confidential for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law.
confidence_note: Based on 130 listed findings across numerous counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward defined terms, mutual notice termination, and post-termination confidentiality survival.

title: Assignment, Transfer and Change-of-Control Consent
where_to_look: Review the assignment, transfer, delegation, successors-and-assigns, and change-of-control provisions.
required: Require prior written consent for any assignment, transfer, delegation, or direct or indirect Change of Control, with consent not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
fallback: Accept prior written consent with a not-unreasonably-withheld-or-delayed standard, even without Affiliate or asset-sale exceptions.
escalate_if: Escalate an absolute consent veto. Escalate any consent-free Change of Control or transfer outside a defined Affiliate or substantially-all-assets exception.
flag_if: The clause requires prior written consent for assignment or transfer.
The clause covers a direct or indirect change of control.
The clause states that consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
The clause states that consent shall not be unreasonably conditioned.
The clause contains an Affiliate or substantially-all-assets exception.
preferred_language: Neither Party may assign, transfer, or delegate this Agreement, in whole or in part, or undergo a Change of Control, without the other Party’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided, however, that a Party may assign this Agreement without consent to any of its Affiliates or to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and this Agreement shall bind the Parties’ permitted successors and assigns.
confidence_note: Based on 55 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward a reasonableness standard, with limited support for Affiliate and asset-sale exceptions.
